title: Inside City Hall: ALU, Control Unit and Registers
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: What does CU stand for?
Choose the model answer: What is the ALU?
Choose the model answer: What does ACC typically store?
Choose the model answer: A full adder has A=1,B=1 and carry-in=0. What are Sum and carry-out?

blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Control Unit generates control signals and interprets the fetched instruction. It is not the component that performs arithmetic itself.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: ALU completes arithmetic and logic such as addition and comparisons; the ACC may hold a result in an accumulator-style model.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Registers serve distinct roles: PC next instruction, MAR memory address, MDR transferred contents, CIR current instruction, ACC intermediate calculation.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model response
blocks.text: ACC holds intermediate result, not memory address.

blocks.title: Model response
blocks.text: Do not say PC is overwritten by subtraction; it tracks instruction address.
